example:
In a shallow clone with no history beyond the last commit, each window holds
only the files' contents on disk and in that commit. `habeas status` says that
coverage history is incomplete and warns about items those contents do not
cover. {test}`requirements.references.coverage.history`
rationale:
**Gap: no test covers the `habeas status` outcome.** The example's expected outcome is that `habeas status` says coverage history is incomplete and warns about the uncovered items. Only the second half is tested.

The only test is `tests/coverage.rs#fn[a_shallow_clone_uses_the_history_it_has_and_says_so]`. Its setup is good:
- It builds a two-commit repository where the first commit's evidence reads `parse` and the second no longer does.
- It makes a real `git clone --depth 1`.
- It asserts that `warned(&target)` is `["parse", "render", "helper"]`, so the window held only the on-disk and last-commit contents and `parse` is uncovered.
- It asserts that the full-history repository still covers `parse`.

That second half of the outcome, the warnings, is covered. The incompleteness note is not covered for `habeas status`. The test calls `habeas::coverage_warning_lines`, defined in `src/commands.rs#fn[coverage_warning_lines]`, which feeds the notice that `habeas author` prints. It asserts that a line containing "coverage history is incomplete" appears in that output.

The `habeas status` output is built separately, in `src/commands.rs#fn[coverage_warnings]`. That function emits the "Coverage history is incomplete…" sentence in the "Coverage warnings" section, and it is called from `status_markdown_with_github`. No test I found exercises that path with a shallow clone:
- `tests/commands.rs#fn[status_preserves_repository_wide_rust_findings_in_every_form]` checks only the "Coverage warnings" heading and an item line, in a non-shallow repository.
- No test searched under `tests` asserts the status "incomplete" sentence.

The shared logic is in `src/coverage_history.rs#fn[warnings]` and `RecentCoverage::load`. The test exercises it, but not the status rendering of the incompleteness statement that the example names.

So the status-specific expected outcome has no assertion, and the example is not fully covered by its tests.

text: :::{example} coverage.shallow_clone
In a shallow clone with no history beyond the last commit, each window holds
only the files' contents on disk and in that commit. `habeas status` says that
coverage history is incomplete and warns about items those contents do not
cover. {test}`requirements.references.coverage.history`
:::{req} coverage.history
An item has recent coverage when it has a reference that covers it under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`, or when its outline node, or
an outline node containing it, is named by file and selector in the inputs of
any version of an existing evidence record, citation review, or site review in
its coverage window. A file's coverage window MUST be its current contents on
disk, committed or not, together with its contents in each of the last N
commits in its Git history that changed it, read through a Git library rather
than by running `git`. A recorded hash MUST NOT matter here: an earlier version
names the node, whatever its code was then. N MUST be the workspace
`[coverage]` setting `reauthorings`, a positive integer, and 3 when it is not
set. When the history is unavailable, such as outside Git or in a shallow clone
missing those commits, the window MUST be the commits that are available, and
the commands of {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.report` MUST say that
coverage history is incomplete.
